topics: Introduction to Smart Grid: Evolution of electric grid
Opportunities and barriers of smart grid
Difference between conventional grid and smart grid
Concept of resilient and self- healing grid
Impacts of smart grid on system reliability
Present development and international policies in smart grid
Information and Communication Technology in Smart Grid: Wired and wireless communication -radio mesh, ZIGBEE, 3G, 4G and 5G
Digital PLC, DSL, Wi-Max, LAN, NAN, HAN, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Li-Fi
Introduction to IEC 61850 standard and benefits
IEC Generic Object-Oriented Substation Event - GOOSE
Smart grid Technologies Part I: Introduction to smart meters
Real Time Pricing- Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) - System, Services and Functions
Smart energy efficient end use devices
Intelligent Electronic Devices (IED) and their application for monitoring & protection: Digital Fault Recorder (DFR)

Wide Area Monitoring System (WAMS), control and protection systems (Architecture, components of WAMS, and applications: Voltage stability assessment, frequency stability assessment, power oscillation assessment, communication needs of WAMS, remedial action scheme)
Smart grid Technologies Part II: Smart substations
Introduction to Smart distributed energy resources and their grid integration
Need and application of microgrid – Energy Management- Role of technology in demand response- Demand side management
Cloud computing in smart grid: Private, Public and hybrid cloud
Types of cloud computing services- Software as a Service (SaaS)
Cyber Security  - Cyber security challenges and solutions in smart grid
Power Quality Management in Smart Grid - Fundamentals
Power Quality (PQ) & Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) in smart grid
Power quality conditioners for smart grid

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module.  Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks. Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered.  Each question can have a maximum of 3 sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Explain the basic concept of distributed energy resources, micro-grid and smart grid
Choose appropriate Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in smart grid
Select infrastructure and technologies for consumer domain of smart grid
Select infrastructure and technologies for smart substation and distribution automation
Formulate cloud computing infrastructure for smart grid considering cyber security
Categorize power quality issues and appraise it in smart grid context
